raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Enable eager ROCm prefill context parallelism for the text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash path in Model Runner V2, using the existing shared PCP metadata and attention logic.

This builds on [#59857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59857) and [#60946](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60946).

## Claims

- Enables PCP for the `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend in eager mode.
- Gathers routing input IDs after local Engram/sequence-parallel preparation
  when expert parallel is disabled.
- Uses the shared sequential attention path under PCP and restores ROCm
  auxiliary streams even when attention raises.
- Rejects unsupported graph, parallel, cache, speculation, and kernel
  configurations at startup.
- A PCP rank with no decode rows returns an empty ragged top-k and skips the
  fused packer, instead of calling `reshape(..., -1)` on a 0-element tensor.
- `forward_mqa` zeros the PCP-padded token tail the same way CUDA FlashMLA
  does. On a gfx950 MXFP8 output that zeros both `data` and `scale`.

## Validation

Rerun on this commit with the checkout `.venv`:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py -v
33 passed, 1 warning in 12.80s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k 'zero_token_pcp_rank or v41_pcp' -v
8 passed, 4 skipped, 211 deselected, 1 warning in 3.32s
```

The four skips require CUDA/Triton. Pre-commit was not re-run: the installed
pre-commit 2.17.0 rejects this repo's hook config (`stages: pre-commit`), and
ruff is not installed in the checkout venv. Added lines are within the 88
character limit. No commit hook is installed in this worktree.

### GSM8K

lm-eval 0.4.13, GSM8K, 1319 samples, 5-shot, greedy (`temperature` 0).
Scores are copied from
`/work/home/hc/deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/results_2026-10-27T18-06-18.974398.json`:

| filter | exact_match | stderr |
| --- | --- | --- |
| strict-match | 0.9249431387414708 | 0.007257633145486643 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9241849886277483 | 0.007291205723162599 |

A short `/v1/completions` check on that server, prompt `The answer to 1+1 is`,
`max_tokens` 16, `temperature` 0, returned ` 2.`.

Server shape:

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100` (engine log:
  `v0.32.1rc1.dev276+gdf6603f05`)
- Local model `/data/hf_hub_cache/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, served as
  `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`
- TP=1, PCP=2, PP=1, DP=1, DCP=1
- Eager, block size 64, max model len 8192
- Prefix caching off, async scheduling off
- `--attention-backend ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`
- FP8 indexer (`indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`) with `indexer_sparse_logits` false
- No monokernel (`kernel_config.monokernel=False`)
- No separate MXFP4 mode was selected. The checkpoint's routed experts still
  loaded as FP4: the log reports `expert_dtype` fp4 and `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`
- `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6,7`
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`

The empty-owner top-k fix from this branch was mounted into the container
(`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` and
`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) and was required. Without
it, `Worker_PCP1` crashed on `reshape` of a 0-element tensor into `[0, -1]`.
Earlier launches died on that reshape before any tokens; those runs are not
this result.

The padded-row zero in `forward_mqa` was added after this GSM8K run, so the
score does not cover it. Expert parallel and a TP=1, PCP=1 comparison were
not run. This remains a draft. A human submitter must review every changed
line before it is marked ready.

## Details

The AMD model previously rejected PCP before constructing its ROCm sparse MLA
attention. The ROCm backends inherit the shared V4.1 PCP metadata builders, so
this change declares that capability and wires the AMD model into the existing
path. No ROCm graph rewriting, HIP capture/replay, DSpark, bounded replay,
prefix-cache, NIXL, Kimi K3, or DeepSeek V4 behavior is changed.

PCP shards decode requests. The rank that owns no rows receives a 0-element
index buffer. `reshape(n, -1)` cannot infer a width from zero elements, and
the exception leaves the other rank blocked in the shared-memory broadcast.
That rank now returns the empty ragged triple the decode path already accepts,
and `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` returns before the same reshape.

PCP also pads each rank's batch. `forward_mqa` now follows CUDA FlashMLA
(`nvidia/flashmla.py`: real tokens are `num_decode_tokens + num_prefill_tokens`,
the tail is `zero_()`'d, and a zero-token step returns). Kernels write only
the real rows, so the tail was uninitialized when inverse RoPE read the bf16
output and when gfx950 consumers read MXFP8 `data` and `scale`. The MXFP8
branch zeros both buffers. The review thread is answered in a reply and left
open.

This does not duplicate an open PR. A search on 2026-10-27 still found no
other AMD eager DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP implementation.
[#61555](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61555) is CUDA decode-only
graph work. [#64135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64135) is ROCm
native ASM sparse attention for DP, not this eager PCP path. The branch was
not rebased; existing merge conflicts with main remain.


---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body:
This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @haic0.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

PCP now goes through our `forward_mqa`, which never zeros the padded rows. CUDA does ([lines 149–156](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2de0531d81525b3fd652ca2f89810b2ff038395e/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashmla.py#L149-L156)). The kernels only fill the real tokens, so that padding is still garbage when it is read later: inverse RoPE on the bf16 path, and the MXFP8 `data` and `scale` on gfx950. Could we clear that tail in `forward_mqa` the same way?

`forward_mqa` now clears the PCP tail the same way CUDA FlashMLA does (`nvidia/flashmla.py`: real rows are `num_decode_tokens + num_prefill_tokens`, that tail is `zero_()`'d, and a zero-token step returns). The bf16 output is cleared before inverse RoPE. On gfx950, the MXFP8 output clears both `data` and `scale`.

This is in c6a1fd05594630226aa56f90c0d9085af288346a. The GSM8K run predates this zeroing, so that score does not cover it. Leaving the thread open.

@@ -16,6 +16,28 @@ Depending on the use case, there are two possible strategies:
 
 Both approaches are under active development.
 
+### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ROCm
+
+ROCm supports eager prefill context parallelism for the text-only
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model with Model Runner V2 and the
+`ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` attention backend:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
+  --language-model-only \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
+  --attention-backend ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
+  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+  --enforce-eager
+```
+
+This configuration requires PP=DP=DCP=1 and does not support microbatching,
+speculative decoding, KV transfer, prefix caching, MegaMoE, the ROCm
+monokernel, LoRA, or multimodal inputs. CUDA/HIP graph support is not enabled
+for this path. TP and PCP multiply, so TP=2 with PCP=2 requires four GPUs.
+
 ## Decode Context Parallel
 
 Due to the auto-regressive nature of decoding, every decoding step needs to compute a small amount of query tokens w.r.t. a large number of key/value tokens stored in the paged KV cache. The core of decode context parallel is how to shard the KV cache across GPUs.

inline_comments.body: PCP now goes through our `forward_mqa`, which never zeros the padded rows. CUDA does ([lines 149–156](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2de0531d81525b3fd652ca2f89810b2ff038395e/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashmla.py#L149-L156)). The kernels only fill the real tokens, so that padding is still garbage when it is read later: inverse RoPE on the bf16 path, and the MXFP8 `data` and `scale` on gfx950. Could we clear that tail in `forward_mqa` the same way?

`forward_mqa` now clears the PCP tail the same way CUDA FlashMLA does (`nvidia/flashmla.py`: real rows are `num_decode_tokens + num_prefill_tokens`, that tail is `zero_()`'d, and a zero-token step returns). The bf16 output is cleared before inverse RoPE. On gfx950, the MXFP8 output clears both `data` and `scale`.

This is in c6a1fd05594630226aa56f90c0d9085af288346a. The GSM8K run predates this zeroing, so that score does not cover it. Leaving the thread open.
